values.AssociatedLNGNotes: An LNG Prime article from December 2021 says Enterprise started service on the Gillis Lateral to serve the growing Gulf Coast LNG market. It says the lateral connects to third party pipelines that serve LNG export facilities.

verifications.note: Names the Gillis Lateral and ties it to interconnects with pipelines serving LNG export facilities.

records.researcher_notes: The source names no single terminal, so the terminal cell stays blank. Enterprise is quoted saying the lateral is fully subscribed with long-term firm shipper commitments.

values.AssociatedLNGNotes: A US Department of the Interior press release says the 807-mile Alaska LNG pipeline is part of a project to move natural gas for export to foreign markets. The pipeline runs from Prudhoe Bay to the liquefaction plant at Nikiski.

verifications.note: Describes the 807-mile Alaska LNG pipeline as part of a project to transport gas for export to foreign markets.

records.researcher_notes: Keeps the yes and terminal already on the sheet and adds a ref. The page does not name Nikiski, which comes from the Energy Information Administration project notes.

ledger.note: A 2021 LNG Prime article ties the Gillis Lateral to pipelines serving LNG export facilities. No single terminal is named.

The Energy Information Administration LNG text for the Acadiana Project is a Kinder Morgan project, not this legacy system. The LNG expansions on this system are the Gillis Lateral and the Haynesville Extension, which are separate rows. Nothing found tying the main line itself to LNG.
Access South is a Texas Eastern expansion moving gas from Pennsylvania to Mississippi. One search found no LNG tie. Texas Eastern LNG links found were for other projects in Louisiana.
Sources describe takeaway from the Delaware Basin to the Waha hub. The LNG link found is only that gas can reach the Gulf Coast through other pipelines, which is not a tie for this project.
The Carlsbad Gateway carries residue gas from a Carlsbad plant to Waha through Agua Blanca. No LNG tie found in the Energy Information Administration text or in two searches.
Existing yes and Alaska LNG Terminal confirmed with a Department of the Interior press release that names the pipeline and export purpose.
The cancelled TransCanada and ExxonMobil line ran to Alberta. The LNG text in the Energy Information Administration data is about the separate Alaska LNG pipeline.
The in-state line is described as a backup plan if the Alaska LNG project is not built. It serves Alaskans, not export. No tie found.
